dedupe_keys.name: simulation of industrial electrical load shapes siels 2018

description: SIELS is a set of simulated electricity demand profiles for manufacturing, aggregated to state level for the year 2018. Each file represents one manufacturing subsector defined by a subset of NAICS codes, and the profiles describe how electricity consumption of that subsector is shaped over the year. The dataset was published on Mendeley Data by Sam Murthy, Sarah Smith, Ikenna Okeke and Alexander Hubbard; version 2 appeared on 6 September 2026 as one downloadable ZIP archive of about 27 MB, free under CC BY 4.0. The page read does not name the country, but NAICS is the North American industry classification, so the states are most likely U.S. states (inferred). Caveats: the profiles are model outputs, not metered data, the time step and simulation method are not stated on the page read, and only 2018 is covered. For simulation it offers ready-made industrial load shapes by subsector and state to fill the industrial part of electricity demand in power system, resource adequacy and outage impact models where metered industrial data are missing. Related catalogue records include the South Korean factory electricity and demand response data, the End-Use Load Profiles for the U.S. Building Stock and the NREL industrial facility combustion energy use data.
